target: The annulus (a thickened ring at the mouth of the perianth tube; there is no PO term for it) is absent. Aristolochia has no corolla: the funnel-shaped organ is the calyx-derived perianth, perianth PO:0009058
fix: 'annulus absent' and 'ring absent' deny only that ring or thickening on the perianth or corolla. They must never become an absence of the organ that bears the ring. Without a term for the ring, hold the absence back. In Aristolochia, map the flower tube to perianth, not corolla.
reason: The perianth is described as funnel-shaped, so only the annulus is missing.

target: fruit septum PO:0025268 not attached to (unfused from, PATO:0000651) fruit valve PO:0000033. Nothing is absent
fix: 'not attached to <part>' and 'free from <part>' describe how a part is attached. They are never an absence of the subject or of the named part. Read them as 'unfused from' or hold them back.
reason: The capsule is described (ovoid). The phrase is about the septa coming free from the valves.

target: fruit septum PO:0025268 unfused from (PATO:0000651) fruit valve PO:0000033. Also, 'septa entire' belongs to fruit septum PO:0025268, not fruit
fix: Same rule: 'not attached to X' describes attachment, not absence. A quality in a 'septa ...' clause goes to the fruit septum, not the whole fruit.
reason: The septa exist (they are entire). They are simply free from the valves.

target: fruit septum PO:0025268 absent PATO:0000462. The fruit PO:0009001 is present (globose)
fix: 'septa absent' or 'septum absent' in a fruit or capsule statement means fruit septum PO:0025268 is absent. 'septa' is a lexicon synonym of septum PO:0000030 and must never fall back to the fruit.
reason: The capsule is described as globose. Only its partitions are missing.

target: Colleters (glands; there is no PO term) on the leaf lamina PO:0020039 are absent. The lamina itself is present (mucronate)
fix: In '<place adjective> <structure> absent' ('laminar colleters', 'petiolar glands', 'marginal spines'), the absent thing is the noun. The adjective only says where it is. Never assign the absence to the place.
reason: 'Laminar' says where the colleters are. The blade is described.

target: The column foot (the base extension of the orchid gynostemium; there is no PO term) is absent. The column is present (clavate). The orchid column is not the style PO:0009074
fix: In Orchidaceae, 'column' means the gynostemium, and 'column foot', 'column wings' and similar are its parts. Map neither to style. Hold the record back until a gynostemium term exists, and never record 'style absent'.
reason: Both statements are about the column. Only its foot is missing.

target: The secondary bracts (bract PO:0009055 of a higher order) are generally absent. The primary bracts are present and glaucous. 'glaucous' should be glaucous PATO:0104277, not green
fix: 'secondary bracts', '2d order bracts' and 'bracteoles' denote a different order of bract. Their absence never removes the primary bracts. Keep the order as the context. 'generally absent' also gives only a variant.
reason: The primary bracts are described. 'Generally' marks it as variable.

target: Leaves on the rhizome (nearest term is rhizome scale leaf PO:0025278) are absent. The cauline leaves (leaf PO:0025034) are present and petiolate
fix: '<position> leaves absent' ('rhizomal', 'basal', 'cauline', 'rosette') denies only that kind of leaf. Keep the position (rhizome, FLOPO:0991002 basal, ...) as the context, and never record 'leaf absent'.
reason: Cardamine constancei has cauline leaves only. The petiolate statement is about them.

target: Basal leaf sheaths PO:0020104 (or scale leaves PO:0006003) have no blade: lamina absent only on the basal leaves. Leaf lamina PO:0020039 on the other leaves is present
fix: 'bladeless' in a statement about basal or proximal sheaths, especially in Cyperaceae and Poaceae, means those basal leaves have no blade (they are cataphylls). It never means a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'. Keep 'basal/proximal leaves' as the context.
reason: The blades are described (glabrous adaxially). 'Bladeless' belongs to the basal sheaths.

target: Basal leaf sheaths PO:0020104 are bladeless (lamina absent on the basal leaves only). 'basal sheaths maroon' belongs to leaf sheath PO:0020104, not leaf
fix: 'bladeless' means the blade is missing, never the leaf. Its scope is the basal sheaths named in the clause. Also map 'sheaths' to leaf sheath PO:0020104.
reason: Carex castanea has normal blades. Its basal sheaths are bladeless and maroon.

target: awn PO:0025349 on the pistillate scales (bract PO:0009055) absent PATO:0000462. The scales are present
fix: 'awns absent', 'awnless' or 'without awns' in a scale, bract, glume or lemma statement means the awn PO:0025349 is absent, never the bearer.
reason: The scales are described (equalling the perigynia). Only their awn tips are missing.

target: vascular bundle PO:0005020 that is part of perigynium PO:0009044 absent (perigynia veinless). The leaf veins are present
fix: 'veinless' or 'nerveless' applies to the subject of its clause (here perigynia). Record vein absence with that bearer and never as a taxon-wide 'vascular bundle absent'.
reason: The subject is 'Perigynia'. The leaf midvein is described separately.

target: Basal leaf sheaths PO:0020104 are bladeless (maroon). Leaf lamina PO:0020039 on the other leaves is present (pilose abaxially)
fix: Same as 'bladeless sheaths': the scope is the basal or proximal sheaths, never all leaves.
reason: 'basal sheaths maroon, bladeless' has the basal sheaths as its subject. The blades are described.

target: leaf sheath PO:0020104 not spotted (PATO:0000333 spotted, negated, so no positive annotation). The sheath is present (apex yellow)
fix: 'lacking <surface feature>' ('lacking spots', 'lacking hairs', 'lacking glands') denies the feature, never the bearer. Record it as the absence of that feature or of that quality, or drop it.
reason: The sheaths are described. Only spots are lacking.

target: Basal sheaths (leaf sheath PO:0020104 of the basal leaves) are bladeless. Leaf lamina PO:0020039 elsewhere is present (convolute or revolute)
fix: 'bladeless <part>' used as an adjective limits the absence to that part. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The blades are described. Only the basal sheaths lack blades.

target: The sheaths of the proximal leaves (leaf sheath PO:0020104) are bladeless. Leaf lamina PO:0020039 of the other leaves is present (papillose abaxially)
fix: 'sheaths of proximal/basal leaves bladeless' limits the absence to those leaves. Keep 'proximal leaves' as the context.
reason: The clause names the proximal leaves. The distal blades are described.

target: Axillary leaf tufts (short shoot PO:0004701 in the leaf axils, FLOPO:0991000 axillary) absent. Leaf PO:0025034 is present (apex acute)
fix: 'tufts/fascicles/clusters of leaves absent' denies the short shoots or leaf clusters, never the leaves. Map it to short shoot PO:0004701, or hold it back.
reason: The absent thing is the axillary tufts. The leaves themselves are described.

target: On the achene (fruit PO:0009001), the marginal spines are absent and the terminal spine (the persistent style) is present and straight. These are fruit spines, not thorn PO:0025172 (a modified shoot)
fix: Position words on spines ('marginal', 'terminal', 'basal', 'lateral') name different members. The absence of one never removes the others. Do not map fruit spines or emergences to thorn.
reason: Ceratophyllum fruits are described by their terminal, basal and marginal spines separately.

target: 'longer ones 1-2 mm' refers to the earlier plural noun, probably the involucral teeth or tepals, not to the awns. The awns are absent
fix: Anaphoric 'ones' ('longer ones', 'inner ones') takes its noun from the clause head, not from the nearest part word, and never from a part stated as absent in the same sentence. Without a clear head noun, hold the record back.
reason: A length for an absent awn cannot be meant. The measurement belongs to the teeth it compares.

target: Basal leaves (FLOPO:0991002 basal) are sometimes absent. When present they are petiolate
fix: Frequency words ('sometimes', 'rarely', 'often', 'generally', 'usually') with 'absent' give a variant, not a taxon-wide absence. Record them as variable or drop them, and keep the leaf kind ('basal') as the context.
reason: The text itself says 'sometimes'. The petiolate leaves are the basal ones when present.

target: 'spineless' applies to another organ (most likely the fruit or a set of areoles). The stem areole spines (spine leaf PO:0025173, not thorn) are present and erect or spreading
fix: In Cactaceae, 'spineless' in a fruit, flower, ovary or tubercle clause applies to that organ only. Map cactus spines to spine leaf PO:0025173, not thorn PO:0025172.
reason: Cylindropuntia munzii is a spiny cholla. The spineless statement must be about another organ.

target: Second-order bracts (bract PO:0009055 of the secondary rays) are absent. The primary inflorescence bracts PO:0009054 are present (greenish or brownish)
fix: '<n>d/second-order bracts absent' denies only that order of bract. Keep the order as the context, and never record 'bract absent'.
reason: The primary inflorescence bracts are described.

target: Inflorescence rays (inflorescence branches, no lexicon term; the head is sessile) are absent. The bracts PO:0009055 are present (the longest erect)
fix: In Cyperaceae and Apiaceae, 'rays' means the inflorescence branches. 'rays absent' means a sessile head, never that the bracts are absent.
reason: The bracts are described. 'Rays' are the inflorescence branches.

target: Leaves are present but reduced and inconspicuous (scale leaf PO:0006003 or reduced leaf). The plant only looks leafless
fix: Hedges like 'seemingly', 'apparently', 'essentially' or 'nearly leafless' mean reduced or inconspicuous leaves, never absent ones. Record 'reduced/inconspicuous' or drop the absence.
reason: The text hedges ('seemingly'), and the other statement says inconspicuous.

target: vascular bundle PO:0005020 that is part of fruit septum PO:0025268 absent. The fruit valves PO:0000033 have a midvein
fix: '<part> not veined/veinless' limits the vein absence to that part. Keep the bearer and never record a taxon-wide 'vascular bundle absent'.
reason: The septum lacks veins, but the valves each have one. These are different parts.

target: The corolla ring (the thin, wavy ring at the corolla tube base; there is no PO term) is rarely absent, so the absence is only a variant. The corolla PO:0009059 is present
fix: 'ring absent' denies only the ring on the corolla or perianth tube, never the corolla. 'rarely absent' gives a variant, so never record a taxon-wide absence from it.
reason: Both statements are about the ring, which is normally present. The corolla is not in question.

target: 'branches not twisted' refers to the inflorescence branches (cyme branches) and is a negated quality: it is not torsioned PATO:0002445. The axillary vegetative branches are absent
fix: A 'branches' clause inside an inflorescence statement belongs to the inflorescence branches, not branch PO:0025073. 'not <quality>' must never be annotated as the positive quality.
reason: In Dudleya, 'branches not twisted' describes the cyme branches. The absence is about axillary shoots.

target: axillary shoot system PO:0006343 ('axillary branch' is a lexicon synonym) absent. The stem (caudex) PO:0009047 is present and branching apically
fix: 'axillary branches absent' maps to axillary shoot system PO:0006343 absent, using the lexicon synonym. It must never fall back to 'stem absent'.
reason: The caudex is described as branching. Only the axillary branches are missing.

target: Basal spikelets (spikelet PO:0009051 in a basal position, FLOPO:0991002) are absent. The terminal spikelet is present (laterally compressed or terete)
fix: 'basal/axillary/lateral spikelets absent' denies only spikelets in that position. Keep the position as the context, and never record 'spikelet absent'.
reason: Eleocharis has one terminal spikelet. Some species also have hidden basal spikelets, and this species does not.

target: bract PO:0009055 on the peduncle PO:0009053 absent PATO:0000462. The involucral bracts PO:0009045 (phyllaries) are present (glabrous abaxially)
fix: In Asteraceae, 'ebracteate' in a peduncle or head-stalk statement means the stalk has no bracts. It never means the phyllaries are absent. Keep the peduncle as the scope.
reason: The phyllaries are described. 'Ebracteate' applies to the peduncles.
